note: Adjudicated accidental variants: two of punctuation and one of accent. Substantive text agrees across both witnesses with zero variants. The two punctuation rulings go against the Clementine Vulgate, which points both places with a comma; the corpus follows the missal's lighter pointing and its own earlier rulings, and the Vulgate's reading is recorded here so the choice is visible.

adjudicated.ruling: Stress on the antepenult, with DO. Circumdo is a compound of do, dare, whose a is short, so the penult of circumdabo is short and cannot carry the stress; the hand missal's accent would have the reader say the word wrongly. Accents are the accidental class the collation strips before comparing letters (ORTHOGRAPHY.md), so the difference is adjudicated here rather than declared as a corrigendum in the witness.

No comma before the 'et' joining the second object of diléxi, with DO and with the corpus rulings at ordinarium.confiteor w028 and ordinarium.iudica-me w038 and w050: decórem and locum are one pair of objects.

No comma before the 'et' joining the second imperative, with DO — the two petitions rédime me and miserére mei are one breath, and the corpus has ruled the same way for two-member series joined by et.
